title: Policy TTL race causes silent tier downgrade across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported requests suddenly being served by lower-tier/cheaper model variants and cross-region fallbacks during brief config churn. Incident surfaced from a Support escalation where an enterprise customer saw 12% of requests in a 15-minute window routed to a quantized low-capacity model despite Dedicated capacity being available in-region. This ticket tracks the investigation, root cause, fix, and rollout for a policy TTL / sync race that allows stale fallback policies to be applied at the edge.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy routing policy changes including tier priority and region pins to control plane.
2) Simulate a transient control-plane reconciliation delay (~20-40s) by blocking policy push to edge nodes.
3) At the same time, trigger capacity scaling events (Dedicated pool burst and deallocation) to change available model variants.
4) Observe that some edge nodes evaluate a fallback policy based on expired TTL metadata and select low-tier model variants for new requests.
5) Verify by checking request traces: route_decision shows policy_version mismatch between control plane and edge, and fallback_reason = "policy_ttl_expired".
Notes: We reproduced consistently when the policy push was delayed and a model capacity change overlapped; simulated with staging fleet using policy sync interrupt script.
impact_summary: Customer-facing misroutes: lower-quality models used for latency-sensitive production traffic across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Manifestations: increased latency (due to cross-region fallbacks), unexpected model quantization artifacts, and billing discrepancies for enterprise customers on Dedicated contracts. Reported by 3 customers during incident window; one enterprise escalated to legal review.
root_cause:
Edge policy evaluator uses a TTL-based fallback marker to decide when to apply fallback rules. During concurrent control-plane policy updates and Dedicated capacity churn, some edge nodes observed a TTL expiry and attempted to apply a fallback computed from stale local policy state because the atomic policy swap did not happen. Contributing factors:
- Non-atomic policy swap: control plane writes new policy metadata in two steps (metadata then versions list), leaving a short window where edge sees inconsistent metadata.
- Policy evaluator permits fallback decisions when local policy_version < control_plane_version AND fallback_TTL < now, rather than fetching the authoritative policy.
- No monotonic version guard on the edge to reject decisions based on stale TTL markers.
- Insufficient observability: traces did not surface policy_version mismatches except via full request logs, delaying detection.
fix_summary: Short-term hotfix (deployed 2026-01-22): change edge evaluator to treat TTL expiry as advisory — when TTL expired and local policy_version != control_plane_version, edge will fetch the latest policy (synchronous fetch) before applying fallback. Long-term fix: implement atomic policy swaps with version monotonicity, add policy_version vector clock on push, and make fallback evaluation idempotent. Add unit/integration tests for overlapping policy update + capacity churn.
rollout_plan: Hotfix rollout: Canary (5% of edge nodes) -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% across regions, with live traffic shadowing to verify no regression (completed 2026-01-22).
Long-term changes: implement atomic policy apply and monotonic version check on edge (branch: feat/atomic-policy-swap), target runtime-1.23 release. Code review and tests in progress.
Private/VPC customers: staged upgrade path and targeted patch notes; coordinate with Solutions for >48h maintenance windows if on-prem patch required.
Dedicated customers with reserved SLAs: offer direct rollback to pre-change configuration and run post-deployment audit reports for affected windows.
testing_and_validation: Added integration test harness that simulates policy push delays and capacity churn; verified no misroutes across 1000 simulated requests.
Added a trace assertion that fails build if a request is routed with policy_version mismatch and fallback_reason = 'policy_ttl_expired'.
Manual verification against the three reported customers' request traces completed; confirmation from SE that requests returned to expected model within canary window.
customer_communication: 2026-01-19: Initial support notification to impacted customers acknowledging issue and providing mitigation steps (route pinning and temporary scaling knobs).
2026-01-22: Hotfix status update and summary of root cause with ETA for permanent fix.
2026-02-01: Postmortem and compensation offer for affected Dedicated customers (credits + SLA review).
action_items: ENG: finish atomic policy apply implementation and land in runtime-1.23 (owner: Liam O'Connor).
SRE: add dashboard for 'policy_version drift' across edge fleet and alert when drift > 3s (owner: Maria Chen).
DX: update Console UI to surface policy_version and last_applied timestamp per route (owner: Priya Nair).
SE/Support: send final customer postmortem and confirm acceptance of compensation (owner: Jordan Li).
notes: Decision: we will not increase TTLs as mitigation because longer TTLs increase risk of stale policy during rapid rollouts.
Trade-off: synchronous fetch on TTL expiry increases tail latency slightly in very rare windows; acceptable vs. customer-impacting misroutes.
Follow-up: evaluate moving to publish/subscribe model for policy changes to reduce push latency and avoid race windows.
